question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Each of the two farmers wants the certified seeds __but neither have any papers.__
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "neither" is a singular pronoun and must be followed by a singular verb. Therefore, "has" should replace "have" in the sentence.
 
• The correct construction is "neither has any papers," ensuring subject-verb agreement.
 
• This rule ensures grammatical correctness and clarity in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Each of the two farmers wants the certified seeds but neither has any papers."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "But either has any papers"** – This is incorrect as "either" refers to one of two and does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "Yet neither has many papers"** – This is incorrect because "many" is used with countable nouns, but "papers" in this context is uncountable.
 
• **Option 4: "Yet none has many papers"** – This is incorrect as "none" does not fit the context of the sentence, which refers specifically to "neither" of the two farmers.
